title: Introduce RBACv2 policy canary + KMS nonce isolation + audit assertion sanitizer
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a staged RBACv2 canary path with non-disruptive enforcement by default; introduces KMS nonce isolation for cross-tenant key usage and an audit assertion sanitizer to remove sensitive PII from logs. Default behaviour is opt-in for tenants; rollout via config flag and canary scaled to 5% then 25% before full rollout.
description: Motivation: We need a low-risk path to validate RBACv2 policy decision changes and a mitigation for KMS nonce reuse that impacted a recent support case (SUP-3314). This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a canary enforcement path for RBACv2 policies that allows simulated decisions to be compared against live decisions before forcing deny/allow; 2) KMS nonce isolation to ensure per-tenant nonces are scoped and never re-used across service proxies; 3) an audit assertion sanitizer that strips or pseudonymizes PII from assertion payloads before they are written to long-term audit storage. The goal is to improve safety, compliance, and our ability to validate policy changes without causing regressions. Implementation summary: - rbac/canary: new middleware rbacv2/canary_router.go and canary_decision_engine.go that fork policy evaluation into a safe sandbox (OPA evaluation with a readonly context) and compare results asynchronously. Decisions are emitted to a new metrics channel (rbac.canary.mismatch) and to a dedicated canary-audit stream. The canary path supports three modes via feature flag: off, simulated, enforce (default rollout uses simulated only). - kms/nonce: introduce kms/nonce_store with tenant-scoped nonce namespaces and a short-lived in-memory ledger backed by Redis. The nonce API guarantees monotonicity per-tenant and rejects reuse attempts with a clear error code (KMS_NONCE_REUSE). Changes touch the KMS client shim and the grpc sidecar that brokers key wrapping. - audit/sanitizer: add audit/sanitizer service (audit/sanitizer.go) applied as a pre-ingest hook. Sanitizer rules are definable via a policy bundle (yaml) with regex + replacement templates; defaults anonymize email addresses, partial account IDs, and SSH keys. The sanitizer emits a hash fingerprint to allow matching without retaining raw values. Rollout and migration plan: - Stage 0 (canary config off): merged to main behind feature flag. - Stage 1 (simulated only): enable canary.simulate=true for 5% of tenant traffic (region + tier sampling) for 7 days. Monitor rbac.canary.mismatch and canary.latency. - Stage 2 (expanded simulation): 25% traffic for 7 days; allow ops to review mismatch traces in the canary-audit stream. - Stage 3 (enforce): flip canary.mode=enforce for tenants that pass policy checks and manual signoff. KMS nonce isolation is enabled as a separate opt-in config per deployment and is safe by default (rejects only suspicious reuse events). The sanitizer is enabled in simulated mode first (it doesn't redact in the primary audit index, only in a secondary sanitized stream) until we validate false positive rates. Testing: - Unit tests: 86 new unit tests for canary router, nonce store and sanitizer rule matcher (coverage + mocks). - Integration tests: add end-to-end test harness that replays historical audit traces through the sanitizer to validate fingerprint stability. - Load tests: canary path uses an async comparator to keep tail latency impact <1ms; perf lab run shows 0.7ms median additional latency at 90th percentile with 1000 rps. Security review: Priya Nair audited KMS changes and confirmed nonce storage is ephemeral and encrypted in transit; Jordan Reyes validated policy-simulation doesn't leak secrets into metrics. Observability: - New metrics: rbac.canary.mismatch, rbac.canary.latency_ms, kms.nonce.rejected, audit.sanitizer.redacted_count - Traces: canary/eval spans, sanitizer/hook spans, kms/nonce span annotation - Dashboard: added RBAC Canary overview and KMS nonce telemetry to Redwood Console under Security > Canary. Migration concerns: - Some legacy tenants rely on raw audit payloads; we default to simulated sanitizer stream; ops will coordinate with customers before full sanitize. - KMS nonce change requires deploy of updated sidecar in Dedicated and Private; upgrade docs added. Related work: builds on policy simulation groundwork (ENG-2107) and addresses the SUP-3314 incident. See Linear SEC-4592 for acceptance criteria. Checklist: - [x] Implement canary router and comparator - [x] Add KMS nonce ledger and API changes - [x] Implement audit sanitizer + default rule set - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Console metrics/dashboards - [x] Docs: migrated examples and upgrade steps (docs/security/rbac-canary.md) - [x] Add feature flag gating and rollout playbook Notes on safety: by default canary is non-enforcing (simulate) so no change to policy outcomes unless explicitly switched. KMS nonce is opt-in per deployment to avoid accidental failures on older clients. The sanitizer defaults to a secondary sanitized stream to avoid loss of raw audit fidelity during validation. Please see the linked dashboards and canary-audit stream for examples of mismatches and sanitizer transformations. Merge strategy: squash-merge. This was validated in a staging rolling upgrade. See CI summaries for passing jobs.
